correctness.rationale: On B_n=K_{1,n} □ P_2, n≥3, let (α,β) be the spine labels and s_i=x_i+y_i be page sums. Feasibility is exactly α+β+Σx_i≥1, α+β+Σy_i≥1, α+s_i≥1, β+s_i≥1, plus each −1 supported by a neighbor 2. A case analysis on α,β∈{−1,1,2} forces total weight at least 4. Equality with spine (2,2) forces every s_i=0 and pages (−1,1) or (1,−1), with |n−2k|≤3 by the global spine bounds. The only other equality spine choices (1,2)/(2,1) require exactly one exceptional page, only feasible for n=3,4,5. Hence M_n=Σ_{|n−2k|≤3} C(n,k)+2n 1_{3≤n≤5}, including M3=14,M4=22,M5=40. A fresh brute checker checks all 3^{2+2n} labelings for n=3,4,5, exactly matching optima and their described families. The symbolic spine/page constraints, not brute force, prove all n.
residual_risks: Only minimum-weight functions on square-page book graphs with n≥3 are counted; not the full feasible weight distribution.

value.rationale: Determining and enumerating every minimum signed Roman function on the canonical n-page book graph is an interpretable combinatorial classification. Its constrained global spine imbalance yields nontrivial central-binomial layers, while the additional Type II optimum structures disappear sharply after five pages; this is a motivated equality-case invariant, not a renaming of the optimum scalar.
